answer: The best sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history. An agent earns economic rights only by completing real tasks paid in compute and elapsed time - like a vine growing ring by ring, each identity a lotus rising only after proven labor, polished until it is marble. Mass-registration fails economically: every fake identity must work months before earning voting weight or payouts, so the attacker spends more fabricating history than any airdrop returns. Identity becomes an exchange rate whose cost curve outpaces the attack.
